chapter: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
title: Wilson's two months on the film and how it portrays Goodman's rise
summary: He worked two months on early Chicago scenes, notes the movie's liberties, and says it ends with the 1938 Carnegie Hall concert.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I was just saying, Teddy, your son is sitting here and if you have any questions, maybe you might want to know something about those times -- how long did it take to make the picture, Teddy? How long were you out there in Hollywood?
Maybe you'd like to ask him something we haven't thought about. I know I'd ask
Let's see, now my part was -- I worked on it two months. And they were scenes of early Chicago, my first entrance into the movie was before Goodman becomes a bandleader ...

PRO-TYPISTS, INC.
PROFESSIONAL TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE
AREA CODE 202 347-5395
-- that little pub that I was supposed to be working at. Because that's not true; I make good money in New York. They take so many liberties in the movie.

And then the next important part in the movie, I guess, they have us doing -- oh, after the band -- that's because the band leader in certain scenes where we're playing at the Palomar Ballroom in Los Angeles, I guess, and the success of the band, and all of a sudden, after flopping along the line, then the tremendous success. And then, of course, the movie ends with the Carnegie Hall Concert in 1938, with the tremendous triumph of the band, the first all jazz concert in Carnegie Hall.
